statement: Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. $M$ and $N$ are midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$. $H$ lies inside $BMNC$; circumcircles of $\triangle BMH$ and $\triangle CNH$ are tangent to each other. The line through $H$ parallel to $BC$ meets these circumcircles at $K$ and $L$. $F = MK \cap NL$, $J$ is the incenter of $\triangle MHN$. Prove $FJ = FA$.

Let $f(x) = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x-2} + \frac{1}{x-4} + \cdots + \frac{1}{x-2018}$ and $g(x) = \frac{1}{x-1} + \frac{1}{x-3} + \cdots + \frac{1}{x-2017}$. Prove $|f(x) - g(x)| > \frac{1}{2}$ for any non-integer $x \in (0, 2018)$.

A collection of $n$ congruent squares is \textit{tri-connected} if: (i) any two touching squares share only a common vertex; (ii) each square touches exactly three others. For $2018 \leq n \leq 3018$, how many values of $n$ allow a tri-connected collection?

From vertex $A$ of equilateral $\triangle ABC$, a ray bounces off the sides following the law of reflection. After $n$ bounces it returns to $A$ without landing on $B$ or $C$. Find all possible values of $n$.
Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with integer coefficients such that if $P(s)$ and $P(t)$ are both integers, then $P(st)$ is also an integer.
